<#
  BlueStick client report — remediation worklist.

  THIS IS THE STARTER TEMPLATE.  Copy this folder to begin your own:
  report-templates/README.md walks through every file.  This one uses the
  smallest template.json there is (title, description, entry, formats), no
  images, no Word styles file (Quarto's default styles) and no
  post-processing script.

  How a template works, in four lines:
    1. BlueStick builds the report's data — sample-data.json is an example.
    2. It fills THIS file with that data using Jinja (delimiters below).
    3. Quarto renders the result to HTML, Word and/or the .qmd source.
    4. Written text (a finding's recommendation…) is added last by a filter,
       so nothing a user typed ever becomes template code.

  The delimiters (spelled out, because writing them here would run them):
    statements   less-than percent  …  percent greater-than   (if, for, set)
    values       two less-thans     …  two greater-thans      (printed, escaped)
    comments     less-than hash     …  hash greater-than      (like this one)

  The rules that keep a report safe — the renderer enforces most of them:
    - A printed value is ESCAPED, so a title such as *bold* prints literally.
    - Written Markdown (description, impact, recommendation…) only through
      md(finding, "field") — never print it as a value.
    - Never print data in the YAML front matter below: Quarto expands
      shortcodes there.  bluestick-meta names the data instead.
    - Never print a value inside `code` or a code block.
#>
---
title: "Remediation worklist"
bluestick-meta:
  title: report.title
  subtitle: report.heading
date: << plain(report.date) >>
engine: markdown
filters:
  - quarto
  - _bluestick/fields.lua
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 2
    theme: cosmo
    embed-resources: true
    include-in-header:
      - text: |
          <style>
          table { width: 100%; }
          mark.bs-todo { background: #ffe066; color: #1a1a1a; padding: 0 .25em; }
          </style>
  docx:
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 2
---

<% if report.draft %>
::: {.callout-warning}
**Draft** — built from the live findings on << plain(report.date) >>. Not for distribution.
:::

<% endif %>
<#
  The data lists FINDINGS, each with the systems it affects.  A worklist wants
  the opposite: SYSTEMS, each with its findings.  This block turns it round.

  - No macros: a macro's output is printed like a value and so escaped.  The
    choice of rows is an inline `set`; reusable layout would be an include.
  - Findings arrive worst first (severity, then CVSS score), so each system's
    findings are listed worst first without sorting.
  - In an addendum only what is new counts: the affected systems of a NEW
    finding, and the NEW systems of a finding reported before.
  - A system whose row says Remediated is already fixed: it is not work.
  - Mutating a dict or list inside a loop (`hosts.update`, `.append`) is how
    Jinja collects across loop iterations; `set` inside a loop does not leak.
#>
<% set rank = {} %>
<% for s in severity_order %><% set _ = rank.update({s: loop.index}) %><% endfor %>
<% set hosts = {} %>
<% set fixes = [] %>
<% for f in findings if f.severity != "info" and f.status == "confirmed" %>
<% if report.kind == "addendum" %>
<% set rows = f.affected if f.change == "new" else (f.new_affected if f.change == "new_hosts" else []) %>
<% else %>
<% set rows = f.affected %>
<% endif %>
<% set open_rows = rows|rejectattr("state", "equalto", "Remediated")|list %>
<% if open_rows %><% set _ = fixes.append(f) %><% endif %>
<% for e in open_rows %>
<% if e.address not in hosts %>
<% set _ = hosts.update({e.address: {"system": e, "rank": rank[f.severity], "items": []}}) %>
<% endif %>
<% set h = hosts[e.address] %>
<% if rank[f.severity] < h.rank %><% set _ = h.update({"rank": rank[f.severity]}) %><% endif %>
<% set _ = h["items"].append({"f": f, "port": e.port}) %>
<% endfor %>
<% endfor %>
<# Worst system first, then by address (sort is stable, so sort twice). #>
<% set worklist = hosts.values()|sort(attribute="system.address")|sort(attribute="rank") %>
# How to use this list

<% if report.kind == "addendum" %>
This addendum to *<< report.baseline.title >>* lists only the work that is new since report << report.baseline.number >>: systems where a new finding was found, and further systems for findings reported before.
<% else %>
Each section below is one system and the findings to fix on it, worst first. How to fix each finding is described once, under **How to fix**, and linked from every system it affects.
<% endif %>

<% if worklist %>
| System | Name | Findings | Worst |
|:------------------|:----------------------------------|:---------|:-----------|
<% for h in worklist %>
| [<< h.system.address >>](#system-<< loop.index >>) | << h.system.name or h.system.hostname or "" >> | << h["items"]|length >> | << h["items"][0].f.severity_label >> |
<% endfor %>
<% else %>
Nothing to fix: no confirmed finding has an open affected system in this report.
<% endif %>

<% for h in worklist %>
## << h.system.address >><% if h.system.name or h.system.hostname %> — << h.system.name or h.system.hostname >><% endif %> {#system-<< loop.index >>}

| Ref | Finding | Severity | Port |
|:------|:---------------------------------------------|:-----------|:------------|
<% for it in h["items"] %>
| [<< it.f.ref >>](#fix-<< it.f.id >>) | << it.f.title >> | << it.f.severity_label >> | << it.port or "" >> |
<% endfor %>

<% endfor %>
<% if fixes %>
{{< pagebreak >}}

# How to fix

<% for f in fixes %>
## << f.ref >> — << f.title >> (<< f.severity_label >>) {#fix-<< f.id >>}

<< md(f, "recommendation", todo="Say what to change to fix it.") >>

<% endfor %>
<% endif %>
<#
  Nothing silently disappears: whatever the worklist left out is named here.
#>
<% set accepted = findings|selectattr("status", "equalto", "accepted_risk")|list %>
<% set remediated = findings|selectattr("status", "equalto", "remediated")|list %>
<% set info = findings|selectattr("severity", "equalto", "info")|list %>
<# Systems already fixed on a finding that is still open elsewhere. #>
<% set fixed = [] %>
<% for f in fixes %>
<% for e in f.affected if e.state == "Remediated" %>
<% set _ = fixed.append({"f": f, "e": e}) %>
<% endfor %>
<% endfor %>
<% if accepted or remediated or info or fixed %>
# Not on this list

| Ref | Finding | Why |
|:------|:---------------------------------------------|:------------------------------|
<% for f in accepted %>
| << f.ref >> | << f.title >> | Risk accepted |
<% endfor %>
<% for f in remediated %>
| << f.ref >> | << f.title >> | Remediated during the assessment |
<% endfor %>
<% for x in fixed %>
| << x.f.ref >> | << x.f.title >> | Already fixed on << x.e.address >><% if x.e.name or x.e.hostname %> (<< x.e.name or x.e.hostname >>)<% endif %> |
<% endfor %>
<% for f in info if f.status == "confirmed" %>
| << f.ref >> | << f.title >> | Informational — nothing to fix |
<% endfor %>
<% endif %>
